name: Everest & Khumbu
tagline: Sherpa villages, high passes and Everest's face
meta_description: Everest and Khumbu treks and tours: Everest Base Camp, Kala Patthar, Gokyo Lakes, Three Passes, heli tours and peak climbs. Prices, seasons, permits.
summary: The Khumbu, in north-east Nepal, is the Sherpa homeland below Everest. Most visitors fly to Lukla at 2,860 m and walk 8–9 days to Everest Base Camp at 5,364 m and Kala Patthar at 5,644 m, or take a 4–5 hour heli tour from Kathmandu. Best months are October–November and March–May.
intro: The Khumbu is the upper valley of the Dudh Koshi and its tributaries, the Imja, Bhote Koshi and Ngozumpa, running north from Lukla to the Tibet border. Everest at 8,849 m, Lhotse, Cho Oyu and Makalu all rise from its rim, and almost all of it lies inside Sagarmatha National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979. There are no roads. Everything moves on foot, by yak or zopkyo, or by helicopter, and the trails link Sherpa villages that have farmed potatoes and traded salt over the Nangpa La for centuries.

Most people come for Everest Base Camp. The standard trek takes 12–14 days from Kathmandu: a 35-minute flight to Lukla, two days to Namche Bazaar at 3,440 m, then Tengboche, Dingboche and Lobuche, with two rest days for acclimatisation, before reaching base camp at 5,364 m and Kala Patthar at 5,644 m for the clearest view of Everest's summit. Walking days run 5–8 hours on good but rocky trails.

Other routes suit other travellers. The 7-day Everest View trek turns round at Namche and Hotel Everest View, staying below 4,000 m. The Gokyo valley holds turquoise lakes and Gokyo Ri at 5,357 m. Strong trekkers link everything over the Cho La, Kongma La and Renjo La on the Three Passes route, and climbers use the trails to reach Island Peak, Lobuche East and Mera Peak. For those who cannot walk, a helicopter tour reaches the Kala Patthar ridge from Kathmandu and returns the same morning.

Accommodation is in teahouse lodges run by Sherpa families, from simple twin rooms with shared toilets at Gorak Shep to heated rooms with attached bathrooms in Namche and Lukla, plus a handful of comfort lodges such as Yeti Mountain Home and Hotel Everest View. Food is dal bhat, Sherpa stew, noodles, potatoes and bakery cakes in Namche. Our packages include Lukla flights, permits, licensed guides, porters and trail meals, priced in INR and USD.

highlights.title: Kala Patthar and Everest Base Camp
highlights.text: From Gorak Shep at 5,164 m, a 2–3 hour walk along the Khumbu Glacier reaches base camp at 5,364 m and the foot of the Icefall. Before dawn the next day, a 2–3 hour climb up Kala Patthar to 5,644 m shows the full south-west face of Everest, which base camp itself cannot see.

highlights.title: Namche Bazaar, the Sherpa market town
highlights.text: Namche fills a horseshoe-shaped bowl at 3,440 m, with lodges, bakeries, gear shops and a Saturday market where traders from lower valleys sell rice and vegetables. Every Everest trek spends two nights here, with a morning climb to Hotel Everest View at 3,880 m for the first close view of Everest and Ama Dablam.

highlights.title: Tengboche Monastery and Mani Rimdu
highlights.text: Tengboche's gompa stands on a forested ridge at 3,867 m with Ama Dablam to the east and Everest at the head of the valley. Monks hold prayers each afternoon that trekkers may attend quietly, and in October or November the Mani Rimdu masked dances fill the courtyard for three days.

highlights.title: Gokyo Lakes and Gokyo Ri
highlights.text: West of the main trail, the Gokyo valley holds six glacial lakes at 4,700–5,000 m beside the Ngozumpa, one of the largest glaciers in the Himalaya. From Gokyo Ri, 5,357 m, four of the world's 8,000 m peaks are visible at once: Everest, Lhotse, Makalu and Cho Oyu. It is quieter than the base camp trail.

highlights.title: Everest by helicopter in a morning
highlights.text: A heli tour leaves Kathmandu at dawn, refuels at Lukla, circles Everest Base Camp and lands on the Kala Patthar ridge for 10–15 minutes, weather and current rules permitting. Breakfast follows at Hotel Everest View at 3,880 m, and you are back in Kathmandu by late morning, after 4–5 hours in total.

highlights.title: Three Passes and trekking peaks
highlights.text: The 20-day Three Passes route crosses Kongma La, Cho La and Renjo La, all above 5,300 m, and visits base camp, Kala Patthar and Gokyo on the way. Climbers use Chhukung and Lobuche as bases for Island Peak at 6,189 m and Lobuche East at 6,119 m, with NMA permits and climbing guides.

getting_there: Almost every Everest trip starts with a flight to Tenzing-Hillary Airport at Lukla, 2,860 m. From Kathmandu it takes about 35 minutes in a 15–19 seat Twin Otter, Dornier or Let aircraft, leaving early in the morning. In the busy months, roughly late March to May and late September to November, scheduled Lukla flights have been moved to Ramechhap (Manthali) Airport, about 130 km and 4–5 hours' drive from Kathmandu, from where the flight takes 20 minutes; departures from Kathmandu often need a 1–2 am pickup. Check current status before you travel. Shared helicopter seats between Kathmandu and Lukla avoid the drive and the small-plane queue. Cloud at Lukla regularly delays flights, so keep one or two spare days at the end of your trip. The overland alternative is a 10–12 hour jeep ride to Salleri or beyond, then two days' walk to Lukla or Surke.
permits: Trekkers need two permits. The Sagarmatha National Park entry permit costs NPR 3,000 plus VAT for foreign nationals and NPR 1,500 for SAARC nationals, including Indians, and is sold in Kathmandu or at the Monjo park gate. The Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality fee, collected at Lukla in place of the TIMS card, was set at NPR 3,000 for most foreigners and NPR 2,000 for SAARC and Chinese nationals from 2024. Nepal's 2023 rule requires foreign trekkers to walk with a licensed guide, though enforcement in the Khumbu has varied. Climbing peaks needs an NMA permit; Mera Peak also needs a Makalu-Barun permit. Check current status before you travel.

months.weather: Namche −8 to 7 °C, Gorak Shep −20 °C at night, dry, very clear
months.summary: January is the coldest month and one of the clearest. Skies are usually blue, trails are almost empty and Lukla flights are more reliable than in spring or autumn. Nights at Lobuche and Gorak Shep fall to around −20 °C, some higher lodges close for a few weeks and snow can block the Cho La and Renjo La. Base camp is possible with a good sleeping bag and a flexible plan. The Everest View trek is a good choice.
months.tip: Bring a sleeping bag rated to −20 °C and a down jacket for January, because lodge bedrooms are unheated.

months.weather: Namche −6 to 8 °C, Gorak Shep −18 °C at night, dry, late-month snow
months.summary: February stays cold but the days lengthen and the air remains clear. Sherpa families celebrate Gyalpo Lhosar, the Tibetan new year, in February or early March, with prayers at the monasteries, new prayer flags and dancing in Namche, Khumjung and Pangboche. Heavy snowfalls are possible late in the month and can close the high passes. Lodges reopen through the month as owners return from Kathmandu for the spring season.
months.tip: Ask your guide which Khumbu villages are holding Lhosar gatherings during your trek, and carry a white khata scarf as a gift.

months.weather: Namche −3 to 12 °C, Lobuche −14 °C at night, clear mornings, afternoon cloud
months.summary: March opens the spring season. Rhododendrons begin to flower around Phakding and below Tengboche, and mornings are usually clear, with cloud building after midday. Nights above 4,500 m are still very cold. From late March the busy-season rule has sent scheduled Lukla flights from Ramechhap, so expect a night-time drive. Expedition teams start arriving, and the passes open as snow settles.
months.tip: Walk early in March, because the clearest views of Ama Dablam and Everest come before 11 am.

months.weather: Namche 1 to 15 °C, Gorak Shep −10 °C at night, warmer, haze builds
months.summary: April is the busiest spring month. Everest expeditions set up at base camp, so the yellow tents along the Khumbu Glacier are at their most crowded, and the trail between Lukla and Namche carries trekkers, porters and yak trains. Days are comfortable, nights cold, and rhododendrons are in full flower below 3,800 m. Haze and afternoon cloud are common, and occasional snow showers dust the high trails.
months.tip: Book Lukla flights and lodges at Lobuche and Gorak Shep at least three months ahead for April.

months.weather: Namche 4 to 17 °C, Gorak Shep −6 °C at night, warm, pre-monsoon cloud
months.summary: May is the warmest month for the high trails and the season of Everest summit pushes, usually in a weather window in mid to late May. Base camp is busy with climbers rather than trekkers. Mornings are still mostly clear at Kala Patthar and Gokyo Ri, but cloud and pre-monsoon showers build earlier in the day by late May, and Lukla flights are cancelled more often. It suits climbers on Island Peak and Lobuche East.
months.tip: Plan May treks to finish by about the 25th, before monsoon cloud starts to close Lukla.

months.weather: Namche 8 to 18 °C, daily rain or drizzle below 4,000 m, cloud
months.summary: The monsoon usually reaches the Khumbu in early to mid June. Rain falls most afternoons and nights below Namche, trails are muddy and cloud hides the peaks for days at a time. Lukla flights are frequently cancelled and many trekkers end up using helicopters. Higher valleys stay drier and green, and lodges along the main trail remain open. We do not sell base camp treks this month.
months.tip: If you must trek in June, keep three spare days for flight delays and buy insurance that covers them.

months.weather: Namche 9 to 18 °C, wettest month, leeches below Phakding
months.summary: July is the wettest month. Cloud sits in the Dudh Koshi gorge, Lukla flights operate only in short breaks, and the trail below Phakding has leeches and landslide-prone sections. Above Dingboche the rain is lighter and wildflowers cover the yak pastures. The Dumje festival, held around midsummer in some Sherpa villages, draws locals home. Views of Everest are rare, so most visitors wait until autumn.
months.tip: Pack leech socks and a full rain shell for July, and expect days with no mountain views at all.

months.weather: Namche 8 to 17 °C, frequent rain, clearer spells late in the month
months.summary: August stays wet, with heavy cloud, unreliable Lukla flights and slippery trails, though rain eases slightly towards the end of the month. The high pastures around Dingboche, Chhukung and Gokyo are green and flowering, and the few trekkers who come have lodges to themselves. Plan a flexible itinerary and expect the peaks to appear only briefly at dawn, if at all.
months.tip: Book a helicopter-backed flight plan in August, because Lukla can stay closed for several days at a time.

months.weather: Namche 5 to 16 °C, Gorak Shep −6 °C at night, rain easing, clearer late
months.summary: September is the shoulder month. The first half can still bring monsoon rain and cancelled flights, but from mid to late September the skies clear, the valleys are green and the trails are quieter than in October. From about 25 September the busy-season Ramechhap rule has applied to scheduled Lukla flights. Late-September starts are a good compromise between weather and crowds.
months.tip: Start a September trek after the 15th if you can, when the monsoon is usually retreating.

months.weather: Namche 2 to 14 °C, Gorak Shep −12 °C at night, dry, very clear
months.summary: October is the best and busiest month in the Khumbu. Skies are usually clear from dawn to mid afternoon, the air is dry after the monsoon and every route is open, including the three passes and Gokyo Ri. Mani Rimdu at Tengboche falls in October or November depending on the lunar calendar. Lodges at Lobuche and Gorak Shep fill up, and Lukla flights run at full capacity from Ramechhap.
months.tip: Book October departures four to six months ahead, because Lukla seats and high lodges sell out first.

months.weather: Namche −2 to 11 °C, Gorak Shep −15 °C at night, clear, colder
months.summary: November brings stable weather, sharp light and colder nights. It is excellent for photography from Kala Patthar and Gokyo Ri, and the trails are slightly quieter than in October. Mani Rimdu at Tengboche often falls in early November. By the end of the month nights at Gorak Shep drop towards −15 °C, and the high passes can collect their first winter snow.
months.tip: Bring a −15 °C sleeping bag and warm gloves for November, and check the Mani Rimdu dates before booking.

months.weather: Namche −6 to 8 °C, Gorak Shep −18 °C at night, dry, clear, cold
months.summary: December is cold, clear and quiet. Most lodges stay open on the main base camp trail, flights are steadier than in peak months and you will share Kala Patthar with very few people. Nights above 4,500 m are bitterly cold, and the Cho La and Renjo La can be icy or snowbound. It is a good month for the Everest View trek and for heli tours, which benefit from settled morning weather.
months.tip: Use microspikes in December for icy sections above Lobuche and on the passes.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for the Everest Base Camp trek?
faqs.a: Plan on 12–14 days from Kathmandu back to Kathmandu. That includes the Lukla flights, about 8 days walking up with two acclimatisation days at Namche and Dingboche, and 3 days walking down. Add one or two spare days for Lukla weather delays. Our 11-day version saves time by flying back from Gorak Shep by helicopter.

faqs.q: How much does an Everest Base Camp trek cost?
faqs.a: Our 12-day Everest Base Camp trek starts from ₹1,22,000 or US$1,390 per person, twin sharing, and the 14-day version from ₹1,40,000 or US$1,590. Prices include Lukla flights, permits, a licensed guide, porters, teahouse lodges and three meals a day on the trail. Kathmandu hotels, insurance and tips are extra.

faqs.q: What permits do I need for the Everest region?
faqs.a: You need the Sagarmatha National Park entry permit, NPR 3,000 plus VAT for foreigners and NPR 1,500 for SAARC nationals including Indians, and the Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality fee, NPR 3,000 for most foreigners and NPR 2,000 for SAARC nationals. TIMS is not used in the Khumbu. Check current status before you travel; our packages include both.

faqs.q: What is the best time to trek to Everest Base Camp?
faqs.a: October and November give the clearest skies and most stable weather. March to May is the second season, warmer and busier at base camp because of climbing expeditions, with more afternoon cloud. December to February is cold but clear and quiet. June to August is monsoon, with rain, cloud and many cancelled Lukla flights.

faqs.q: Can I see Everest without trekking?
faqs.a: Yes. A helicopter tour from Kathmandu flies up the Khumbu, circles base camp and lands on the Kala Patthar ridge for 10–15 minutes when weather and current rules allow, then stops for breakfast at Hotel Everest View. Shared seats start from about ₹1,05,000 or US$1,190. Mountain flights from Kathmandu also pass Everest without landing, for much less.

faqs.q: Why do Lukla flights leave from Ramechhap?
faqs.a: To ease congestion at Kathmandu airport, Nepal's aviation authority has moved scheduled Lukla flights to Ramechhap (Manthali) Airport in the busy months, roughly late March to May and late September to November. Ramechhap is a 4–5 hour drive from Kathmandu, and flights take about 20 minutes. Check current status before you travel; our packages include the transfer.

faqs.q: Is the Everest Base Camp trek hard for beginners?
faqs.a: It is a challenging trek but not a technical one. You walk 5–8 hours a day on rocky trails, gaining up to 800 m, and the thin air above 4,000 m makes everything slower. Fit beginners who train for 6–8 weeks with long uphill walks usually manage. The real risk is altitude, so acclimatisation days are not optional.

faqs.q: Where do you sleep on the Everest Base Camp trek?
faqs.a: In teahouse lodges run by Sherpa families. Rooms are twin-bedded with foam mattresses and blankets; Namche and Lukla lodges often have attached bathrooms and heated dining rooms, while Lobuche and Gorak Shep are basic, with shared toilets. For more comfort, Yeti Mountain Home lodges and Hotel Everest View offer heated rooms on the lower trail.

faqs.q: Can Indian families do an Everest tour with children or parents?
faqs.a: Yes, with the right trip. The 7-day Everest View trek stays below 4,000 m and suits fit teenagers and active older parents. The helicopter tour suits families with mixed fitness, but infants, pregnant women and people with heart or lung conditions should not land above 5,000 m. Base camp itself is best for children over 12 who walk regularly.
